notes:
Summary: Mid-market product org building a dev-centric knowledge assistant and semantic search for customer-facing docs. Initial POC on Hosted API (Nov) looked good for quality; moved to Dedicated evaluation after seeing tail latency spikes under load. Primary ask: predictable p99 latency and cost controls for a customer SLA product.

Highlights / quotes: 
- CTO (Maya Patel): 'We need predictable p99 — can't have noisy tail at 95-99th percentiles for enterprise customers.'
- Head of Product (Oliver): 'Hosted quality was fine but spikes make us nervous; dedicated capacity + KV caching is attractive.'

Technical requirements: 
- Workloads: real-time chat (multi-turn), embeddings for doc search, reranking on top-10 candidates.
- Traffic profile: baseline 30-50 concurrent users, peak bursts up to ~1,000 concurrent requests during marketing events. Target steady-state throughput ~45 QPS, peak burst ~300 QPS.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms (hard requirement).
- Model preferences: open models (Llama-2 style/variants) initially, willing to evaluate quantized variants; care about hallucination/regression monitoring.
- Data & compliance: must support SSO (SAML), SOC2-level controls, customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs, and EU/NA residency for subsets of data.

Commercial / pricing discussion notes: 
- Interested in Dedicated reserved GPU pools. Primary ask is a flexible commit + burst model: commit defined as tokens/day with guaranteed throughput; burst capacity with predictable overage pricing.
- Proposed ramp: month1 commit = 50% of projected steady, month2 = 75%, month3+ = 100% (they want a gradual ramp to fit finance approvals).
- Example ask from customer: commit 200k tokens/day with ability to burst to 1M tokens/day. Want explicit overage cap or tiered overage price to avoid runaway costs during campaigns.
- Pricing sensitivity: mid-market margin pressure — prefer higher commit discounts in exchange for multi-quarter ramp guarantees and a 6–12 month contract.
- Redwood provided two options in deck: (A) 12-month commitment with lower overage rate + burst buffer; (B) 6-month pilot-to-term with variable overage and built-in auto-scale credits. MosaicRoute leaning toward (A) if legal/KMS terms acceptable.

Procurement friction points: 
- Finance wants monthly visibility and a mechanism to convert unused commit credits (carry-forward or crediting) during slow months.
- Legal is negotiating KMS/customer key language and SLAs for p99 latency; they requested Redwood SLAs mapping to committed throughput.
- Ops wants rollout plan for canary + fallback to hosted if Dedicated nodes degraded.

Open action items: 
- SE (Priya) to provide sample SLA doc mapping throughput tiers to expected p99 within 3 business days.
- AE (Evan) to play out two pricing exhibits showing: 1) 12-month commit with 25% discount and capped overage, 2) 6-month ramp with burst credits.
- Send draft term sheet for internal finance by 2025-01-20.
